req.title: Reuse db connection per request
req.statement: The system shall reuse a single sqlite3 connection per Flask request via flask.g.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-025 requires that a single sqlite3 connection is reused per Flask request via flask.g. The key behaviour is: (1) get_db() returns the same object when called twice within the same app context (positive/EP), (2) a new connection is created for a new request context — i.e. connections are NOT shared across requests (boundary/BVA), and (3) after the request teardown close_db() removes 'db' from g so a subsequent call in a fresh context creates a new connection (negative/STC). We also verify the connection is stored under the exact key 'db' in g, and that the returned object is a real sqlite3.Connection. These assertions target mutations that change the key name, skip the g-caching branch, or break the identity check.

tests.name: test_get_db_returns_same_connection_within_single_request_context
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
actions: Push an application context
Call get_db() twice within the same context
Compare the two returned objects with 'is'
expected: Both calls return the exact same sqlite3.Connection object (identity check passes)
The object is stored in g under the key 'db'
The object is an instance of sqlite3.Connection
trace: R-FLASKR-025: reuse single sqlite3 connection per request via flask.g
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db
from flask import g

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite'); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

def test_get_db_returns_same_connection_within_single_request_context():
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        conn1 = get_db()
        conn2 = get_db()
        assert conn1 is conn2, 'get_db() must return the same object on second call'
        assert isinstance(conn1, sqlite3.Connection)
        assert 'db' in g, "connection must be stored in g under key 'db'"
        assert g.db is conn1, 'g.db must be the same object returned by get_db()'

tests.name: test_get_db_creates_new_connection_for_each_new_request_context
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
actions: Push first application context, call get_db(), capture id, pop context
Push second application context, call get_db(), capture id, pop context
Compare the two connection ids
expected: The two connection objects have different ids (they are distinct objects)
Each context yields a valid sqlite3.Connection
trace: R-FLASKR-025: connection is unique per request — a new context must not reuse the previous request's connection
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite'); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

def test_get_db_creates_new_connection_for_each_new_request_context():
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()

    with app.app_context():
        conn1 = get_db()
        id1 = id(conn1)
        assert isinstance(conn1, sqlite3.Connection)

    with app.app_context():
        conn2 = get_db()
        id2 = id(conn2)
        assert isinstance(conn2, sqlite3.Connection)

    assert id1 != id2, 'Different request contexts must not share the same connection object'

tests.name: test_close_db_removes_connection_from_g_so_next_call_creates_fresh_one
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
actions: Push an application context
Call get_db() to create and cache the connection
Call close_db() to simulate teardown
Assert 'db' is no longer in g
Call get_db() again in the same context
Assert a new connection is returned (different object)
expected: After close_db(), 'db' is absent from g
A subsequent get_db() call creates a new sqlite3.Connection
The new connection is a different object from the original
trace: R-FLASKR-025: teardown via close_db() must clear g.db so the caching logic starts fresh
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, close_db, init_db
from flask import g

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite'); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

def test_close_db_removes_connection_from_g_so_next_call_creates_fresh_one():
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        conn1 = get_db()
        assert 'db' in g
        close_db()
        assert 'db' not in g, "close_db() must remove 'db' from g"
        conn2 = get_db()
        assert 'db' in g, "get_db() after close_db() must re-populate g.db"
        assert isinstance(conn2, sqlite3.Connection)
        assert conn1 is not conn2, 'After close_db(), get_db() must return a NEW connection'

actions: Push an application context

Call get_db()

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db
from flask import g

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite'); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

def test_get_db_connection_stored_under_exact_key_db_in_g():
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        assert 'db' not in g, "g must not contain 'db' before get_db() is called"
        conn = get_db()
        assert 'db' in g, "get_db() must store connection in g under key 'db'"
        assert g.db is conn, 'g.db must be identical to the object returned by get_db()'
        assert isinstance(g.db, sqlite3.Connection)
        # Calling again must not change g.db
        conn2 = get_db()
        assert g.db is conn2
        assert conn is conn2

tests.name: test_http_request_yields_200_and_connection_reuse_does_not_corrupt_response
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
actions: Use test_client() to GET '/' (blog index)
Assert HTTP 200
Assert known post title from pre-loaded data appears in response
Make a second GET '/' in the same client session
Assert HTTP 200 again — connection reuse must not corrupt subsequent requests
expected: Response contains pre-loaded post title 'Pulse ember signal'
trace: R-FLASKR-025: connection reuse per request must not corrupt HTTP responses across multiple requests
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite'); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_http_request_yields_200_and_connection_reuse_does_not_corrupt_response():
    client = app.test_client()
    r1 = client.get('/')
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    assert b'Pulse ember signal' in r1.data
    r2 = client.get('/')
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert b'Pulse ember signal' in r2.data

tests.name: test_get_db_row_factory_is_sqlite_row_within_request_context
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp DATABASE path
actions: Push an application context
Call get_db()
Inspect the row_factory attribute of the returned connection
expected: This confirms the connection is fully configured as per db.py line: g.db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
trace: R-FLASKR-025: the cached connection must be configured with sqlite3.Row factory — mutation of row_factory assignment would break column-name access
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite'); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

def test_get_db_row_factory_is_sqlite_row_within_request_context():
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        conn = get_db()
        assert conn.row_factory is sqlite3.Row, (
            'get_db() must set row_factory to sqlite3.Row on the cached connection'
        )
        # Reuse: second call must return same connection with same row_factory
        conn2 = get_db()
        assert conn2.row_factory is sqlite3.Row
        assert conn is conn2
